_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Tonga covering Lapita settlement (~1500 BCE), Tu'i Tonga Empire (950-1865, one of largest Pacific empires, ruled from Samoa to Niue), Ha'a Tui Kanokupolu dynasty, never colonised (only Pacific nation never fully colonised, British protectorate 1900-1970 but retained sovereignty), Christian conversion (King George Tupōu I 1831), Constitution 1875 (one of oldest in Pacific), independence/sovereignty restoration 1970, pro-democracy movement 2006 riots, Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai eruption 2022.

religion.note: Free Wesleyan Church of Tonga (Methodist, largest, royal family's church, closely linked to monarchy since King George Tupōu I's conversion 1831); LDS/Mormons (18%, among highest globally, Liahona High School, returned missionaries, temples); Catholic; Free Church of Tonga (split from Wesleyan); Seventh-day Adventist; Assemblies of God; Sunday strictly observed (constitutionally protected, no commerce/sport/work, most conservative sabbath in Pacific); church donations enormous (10%+ income for most families, pastor system); Christianity is constitutional requirement for monarchy

ethnic_groups.name: Tongan
ethnic_groups.notes: Polynesian; most ethnically homogeneous Pacific nation; monarchy reverence (King holds quasi-divine status, fahu respect system, commoners bow, protocol elaborate); Tu'i Tonga Empire legacy (950-1865, ruled from Samoa/Fiji/Niue/Rotuma, tribute system, Tongan imperialism before European contact); kava ceremony (most important social/political ritual, inu kava, daily practice); tapa cloth (ngatu, bark cloth beaten/decorated, ceremonial); fa'a Tonga ('Tongan Way', similar to fa'a Samoa but with stronger monarchy); obesity (70%+ overweight, highest rates globally alongside Nauru, 'big is beautiful' cultural attitude, now health crisis, diabetes); rugby union and league (national passion, disproportionate international impact, Ikale Tahi, many play for NZ/Australia); strong outmigration; communal values

ethnic_groups.name: Part-Tongan
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed European-Tongan; historically trading families; some prominent in business/politics

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (~few hundred, temporary business), European (~few hundred), other Pacific Islanders; massive diaspora (~80k in NZ, ~30k in Australia, ~60k in US, diaspora roughly equals or exceeds homeland population; remittances ~40% GDP, highest in world by percentage)

independence.from: UK protectorate ended (but Tonga was never colonised; British protectorate 1900-1970 mainly handled foreign affairs, internal sovereignty maintained continuously; Constitution 1875)

country_profile.notes_unique: Never colonised (only Pacific Island nation never fully colonised by European power, British protectorate 1900-1970 but Tongan kings retained sovereignty/governance, Constitution 1875, unique continuous Polynesian monarchy); Tu'i Tonga Empire (c. 950-1865, one of largest pre-European Pacific empires, extended suzerainty over Samoa/Fiji/Niue/Rotuma/Wallis and Futuna, maritime tribute system, monumental architecture, Ha'amonga 'a Maui trilithon 'Stonehenge of the Pacific'); Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai eruption (January 15, 2022, one of most powerful volcanic eruptions in recorded history, VEI 5-6, mushroom cloud 58km high reached mesosphere, tsunami hit Tonga/Peru/Japan/US West Coast, undersea cable severed cutting communications for weeks, 3 deaths Tonga, atmospheric pressure wave circled globe 4 times, global temperature dip 0.035°C, massive SO2 injection); 2006 Nuku'alofa riots (pro-democracy movement, parliament reform demands, CBD burned, 8 dead, Chinese businesses targeted, King's power challenged); monarchy (one of world's last ruling monarchies with real power, King Tupou VI since 2012, constitutional reforms 2010 reduced powers after decades of pro-democracy agitation but king retains significant influence, nobles in Parliament, land tenure controlled by king/nobles/commoners); Constitution 1875 (King George Tupōu I, among oldest written constitutions still in force outside Europe, influenced by missionaries/Sydney advisors, outlawed slavery, guaranteed freedoms); kava ceremony (most elaborate in Pacific, integral to politics/social life/diplomacy); whale watching (Vava'u, humpback whales breeding, eco-tourism); 169 islands (36 inhabited); remittances (~40% GDP, among highest in world, diaspora-dependent); obesity crisis (70%+ overweight, cultural attitudes toward large body size, diabetes epidemic); rugby (Ikale Tahi, punches way above weight, many Tongan-heritage play for NZ All Blacks); tapa cloth (ngatu, women's art, ceremonial importance); Sunday sabbath (enshrined in constitution, strictest in Pacific)

natural_resources.notes: Very limited natural resources; economy heavily dependent on remittances (37% of GDP)

current_leader.name: Hu'akavameiliku Siaosi Sovaleni
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Appointed by King Tupou VI; managed Hunga Tonga eruption aftermath (January 2022, communications cut, reconstruction); COVID response; development; consensus builder

head_of_state.name: King Tupou VI
head_of_state.title: King of Tonga
head_of_state.notes: Tu'i Kanokupolu line; succeeded brother George Tupou V (died 2012); military background; reserves significant constitutional powers despite 2010 reforms; appoints PM and some ministers; nobles in Parliament; popular; Hunga Tonga eruption leadership; maintains Tonga's unique monarchical tradition

former_leaders.name: George Tupou V
former_leaders.notes: Eccentric; Oxford-educated; voluntarily ceded most powers 2010 (democratic reforms, reduced nobles/royal power, major concession); 2006 riots pressure; championed reforms; died 2012; important transitional monarch

former_leaders.name: Taufa'ahau Tupou IV
former_leaders.notes: Longest-reigning (41 years); absolute ruler for most of reign; economic development (satellite registration, passports-for-sale controversies); 2006 riots pressure for reform; died 2006; dominated Tonga's modern era; giant man (130kg+, Guinness World Record heaviest monarch)

former_leaders.name: Queen Sālote Tupou III
former_leaders.notes: Beloved queen; 47-year reign; famous at Elizabeth II's 1953 coronation (rode open carriage in rain, refusing to close as smaller King of Tonga tradition, charmed London); reunified Tongan churches; cultural champion; died 1965; national heroine

former_leaders.name: George Tupou I
former_leaders.notes: Founder of modern Tonga; unified islands through warfare/diplomacy; Christian convert (Methodist, 1831); 1875 Constitution (abolished serfdom, established parliament, rights); resisted colonisation; negotiated protectorate on favourable terms; greatest Tongan king; 'Bismarck of the Pacific'
